text: The Bright Star Catalogue, also known as the Yale Catalogue of Bright Stars, Yale Bright Star Catalogue, or YBS, is a star catalogue that includes all stars of stellar magnitude 6.5 or brighter, which corresponds to roughly every star visible to the naked eye from Earth. The catalog lists 9,110 objects, of which 9,095 are stars, 11 are novae or supernovae that were "bright stars" only at their peak, and four are non-stellar objects: the globular clusters 47 Tucanae (HR 95) and NGC 2808 (HR 3671), and the open clusters NGC 2281 (HR 2496) and Messier 67 (HR 3515). The catalogue has a fixed number of entries, but its data is maintained and continuously updated, with a comments section about the objects being steadily enhanced. The abbreviation for the catalog is BS or YBS, but all citations of stars in it use HR before the catalog number, a tribute to its predecessor, the Harvard Revised Photometry Catalogue, published in 1908. The earliest predecessor, titled Harvard Photometry, was published in 1884 by the Harvard College Observatory under Edward Charles Pickering and contained about 4,000 stars. Pickering then promoted a similar survey for the southern celestial hemisphere, conducted by Solon I. Bailey between 1889 and 1891, resulting in the publication of the Revised Harvard Photometry in 1908, which included stars down to magnitude 6.5 in both hemispheres, a work continued by John A. Parkhurst through the 1920s. The Yale Bright Star Catalogue was first published in 1930 by Yale astronomer Frank Schlesinger; although the number of entries remains fixed at 9,110, the data for listed objects is corrected and extended, and a comments section is appended. The 1991 edition was the fifth in sequence and introduced a significant expansion of the comments section, which grew to just over the size of the catalogue itself. This edition, along with earlier ones, was compiled and edited by Ellen Dorrit Hoffleit of Yale University. The Harvard Revised Photometry, based on visual observations, has been replaced by photo-electric measurements using band pass filters, most notably the UBV photometric system, which can differ substantially—up to 1.8 magnitudes—from the older system. As a result, many stars brighter than V=6.50 are not included in the YBSC, and hundreds of stars in the YBSC are fainter than V=6.50. In 1983, Dorrit Hoffleit, Michael Saladyga, and Peter Wlasuk published a Supplement adding 2,603 stars with V magnitudes brighter than 7.10 measured at that time. The YBS has one predecessor and five editions.
